preamble: In the western and south-central dialects of Asturian and Leonese, the phoneme that standard Asturian realizes as the palatal lateral /ʎ/ (ll, from Latin initial L- and medial -LL-) is pronounced as an obstruent, the 'che vaqueira', written ḷḷ. A common realization is the voiceless retroflex affricate [ʈʂ], reported for Aller, Quirós and other councils; other areas have [ɖʐ], [ɖ] or [ts]. The sources describe these as realizations corresponding to central [ʎ]; whether every che vaqueira area passed through a [ʎ] stage is debated, so the cell rests on the regular ʎ ~ ʈʂ correspondence.

examples.note: Initial L-; standard Asturian has [ʎ], che vaqueira dialects a retroflex affricate.
Listed as a western Asturian che vaqueira form; ḷḷ is [ʈʂ] in Aller and Quirós, [ɖʐ], [ɖ] or [ts] elsewhere.
Medial -LL- gives the same sound (also mueḷḷe 'soft' < Latin molle).
Cited as an example of the ḷḷ digraph in the Asturian alphabet.
